rule: rust-async-background-work rule 5 / checklist 10 ("If a stale result could still land, is it rejected on arrival?") — a cancelled pass must not leave a half-finished artifact behind where the next run will adopt it as complete
summary: `reload` publishes the prepared `DiffModel` into the process-wide LRU cache before the syntax pass runs, so any cancelled or superseded pass permanently caches an un-highlighted model that every later view adopts without ever re-running the syntax job.
failure_scenario: A `DiffView` shows patch A; while its syntax pass is still on the background executor the embedder calls `set_unified(B)` (or the view is dropped — scrolling a list of tool diffs does this routinely). `reload` sets `cancelled`, the A task returns at `if !installed` / `if cancellation.load(...)`, and model A is already in `CACHE` with an all-default `syntax` vector. Any later `DiffView::for_path(_, A, cx)` — reopening the same file, revisiting the same commit, re-rendering the same agent tool diff — hits `cached(key)`, installs the syntax-less model and starts no task, so patch A renders as flat unhighlighted text for the remaining life of the process (or until 16 other diffs evict it).
proposed_fix: Move `retain(key, &model)` to after `target.apply_syntax(runs)` succeeds, or record completeness on the model (e.g. a `syntax_applied: Cell<bool>`) and have `cached()` treat an incomplete entry as a miss so `reload` re-runs the syntax pass for it.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in crates/fleet-lazygit/src/diff_view.rs's test module: build a `DiffView` over a patch whose language resolves, immediately call `set_unified(other_patch)` before `run_until_parked`, then `run_until_parked`, then build a second `DiffView` over the original patch and `run_until_parked`. Assert the second view's model has non-empty syntax runs for at least one payload row. It fails today (the cached model's runs are all default) and passes once the model is only cached after `apply_syntax`.
verify_reason: Verified line by line. diff_view.rs:441 checks cancellation, then :444 `retain(key, &model)` publishes into the thread-local LRU (:56-60, CACHE_LIMIT 16 at :46) before any syntax exists. Both later exits — `if !installed { return; }` (:459) and `if cancellation.load(...) { return; }` (:465, after the syntax `background_spawn` await) — leave the cached Rc with `syntax: RefCell::new(vec![Vec::new(); count])` (views/diff_model.rs:362), and `runs_for` (diff_model.rs:381-389) then returns an empty slice forever, i.e. flat unhighlighted text. reload() short-circuits on a cache hit at :403-406 and spawns nothing, so the poisoned entry is never repaired. Drop (:310-314) and the `self.cancelled.store(true)` at the head of reload (:400) make both exits routinely reachable — dropping a DiffView while its syntax pass is on the background executor is the normal case when a transcript list scrolls. Nothing lazily re-runs syntax at render time.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-lazygit/src/diff_view.rs (retain/cached signatures and the reload task) and crates/fleet-lazygit/src/views/diff_model.rs if completeness is stored on the model; the existing cache-eviction test at diff_view.rs:759-766 calls retain(key, &Rc<DiffModel>) directly and breaks on any signature change. No other crate touches CACHE/retain/cached (both are private to the module).
corrected_fix: Do not simply move `retain` after `apply_syntax`: that also drops caching for the very common drop-mid-pass case, so re-opening the same diff re-runs the whole prepare pass, and two views mounted on the same patch would each prepare independently. Record completeness instead — a `Cell<bool>` on DiffModel set inside `apply_syntax` (diff_model.rs:457) — keep `retain` where it is so the flattened model is still shared, and have `reload`'s cache-hit arm at :403-406 install the cached model *and* still spawn the syntax pass when the flag is false (jobs are recoverable via `DiffModel::syntax_jobs()`, diff_model.rs:398). Cheapest partial mitigation as well: at :465 the runs are already computed, so apply them to `target` even when cancelled and skip only the `cx.notify()` — that removes one of the two poisoning paths for free.

rule: gpui-performance rule 1 + 8 ("CPU work goes to the background executor") + rule 7 ("never a freshly constructed `WindowTextSystem`"); checklist A1/A7/D1
summary: `diff_list` shapes every payload row of the diff model on the foreground thread the first time a model is drawn, through a throwaway `WindowTextSystem` whose shaping cache is discarded — a synchronous hitch proportional to the whole diff, inside the render path.
failure_scenario: Move the file-tree cursor onto a 5 000-line changed file. `build_model` finishes on the background executor and notifies; the very next frame calls `diff_list`, which synchronously shapes all 5 000 payload lines (plus allocating a `Vec<f32>` of 5 000) before a single row is drawn. The window is frozen for the duration — hundreds of milliseconds on a wide diff, far past the 8 ms budget — and because the `WindowTextSystem` is local, none of that shaping is reused by the paint path, which re-shapes the visible rows through the window's own cache anyway.
proposed_fix: Move the measurement into `build_model` / `prepare`, where a `WindowTextSystem` is already constructed on the background executor and the cancellation flag is already checked per row, and store the result on the model before it is installed. `diff_list` then reads `model.payload_advances` and never shapes.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-lazygit/src/views/diff.rs`'s test module a case `payload_advances_are_measured_before_the_model_is_installed`: build a diff model through the background `prepare` path in a `#[gpui::test]`, and assert `model.payload_advances.get().is_some()` immediately after the model lands in the view, before any draw. It fails today because the `Cell` is only filled by the first `diff_list` call.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-lazygit/src/views/diff.rs:418 calls `measure_payload_advances(&model, cx)` at the top of `diff_list`, and :489-521 builds a throwaway `WindowTextSystem::new(cx.text_system().clone())` and `shape_line`s every panned payload row (long lines are skipped because they are pre-shaped, :505-507). The `Cell` guard at :490 makes it once per model, not per frame — the finding says so — but it is once per model *on the foreground thread, inside the render path*, right after `build_model`/`prepare` already walked the same rows on the background executor with a `WindowTextSystem` in hand (root/diff_view.rs:38-52, diff_view.rs:244-265). Rules 1, 7 and 8 all point the same way, and nothing in the code or comments justifies the placement.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-lazygit/src/views/diff.rs:411-418,489-537 (and the test at :596-597 that calls `measure_payload_advances` directly), views/diff_model.rs:167,185,360 (`payload_advances: Cell<Option<[f32; 2]>>` can become a plain field once it is filled at build time), crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/diff_view.rs:28-60, crates/fleet-lazygit/src/diff_view.rs:234-265,405-435 (both prepare paths must be changed together), plus `max_h_scroll`'s fallback at views/diff.rs:474-478.
corrected_fix: Move the measurement into `build_model`/`prepare`, but carry the three theme-derived inputs it needs (`theme.font_mono`, `theme.text.data.size`, and the mode already on the model) explicitly — `long_line::Style::new(cx.theme())` is already resolved on the foreground and handed to the background task, so extend that struct rather than reaching for `cx` off-thread. Check the cancellation flag inside the advance loop the way the long-line loop already does, and keep `max_h_scroll`'s `payload_columns` fallback so a cancelled/legacy model still clamps. Do not drop the `Cell` in the same commit — `DiffModel::build` is constructed in two places plus tests, so land the background fill first and only then tighten the type.

rule: rust-async-background-work rule 8 / checklist 23 ("Does the drain loop batch or yield?" — copy shell/root/events.rs:111-160: batch to a named const, then `timer(1ms).await`)
summary: Lazygit's bridge drain loop batches but never yields, so an always-ready receiver keeps the GPUI foreground executor inside the loop and starves rendering — the exact hazard fleet-app's identical loop guards against with a 1 ms timer.
failure_scenario: The git worker thread emits a burst — a `Snapshot` whose `apply_snapshot` returns follow-up requests that each answer with a `FileDiff`/`CommitDiff`/`Command` event, plus watcher `Changed` events — faster than the loop consumes. Because `recv()` is always ready, the task never parks: the foreground executor stays inside `spawn_event_loop`, GPUI paints no frame and the Lazygit window is unresponsive to keys for the whole burst instead of dropping at most one frame per 64 events.
proposed_fix: Copy the canonical shape: hoist `const EVENT_BATCH_LIMIT: usize = 64;` next to the other consts in root.rs, use it as the batch bound, and end each iteration with `cx.background_executor().timer(Duration::from_millis(1)).await;` with the same comment.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in crates/fleet-lazygit that pre-loads the bridge event channel with (batch limit + 1) `GitEvent`s, spawns the loop, calls `cx.run_until_parked()` once, and asserts that only the first batch has been applied (a counter on the root, or the second batch's effect absent). Today all events are applied in one park because the loop never yields; after the fix the second batch needs `cx.executor().advance_clock(Duration::from_millis(1))` plus another `run_until_parked`.
verify_reason: root/events.rs:9-31 is a `while let Ok(event) = events.recv().await` with a 64-item try_recv batch and no await after the update, so with a non-empty async_channel every iteration resolves on first poll and the whole backlog is consumed inside a single foreground-task poll. It is a `cx.spawn` on Context<Lazygit>, i.e. the foreground executor. fleet-app's counterpart states the rule and yields — shell/root/events.rs:155-158 with `EVENT_BATCH_LIMIT` named at events.rs:16 — and the producer here is unbounded (bridge.rs:384-385) with a worker that can emit a Snapshot plus a burst of ReadSuperseded/diff events back to back (bridge.rs:619-630). The divergence from the documented in-repo shape is real and the fix is mechanical.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/events.rs and a `const EVENT_BATCH_LIMIT` next to the other consts in crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root.rs. Any existing lazygit test that drives events with a single run_until_parked will now need `advance_clock(1ms)` per extra batch — check the tests under crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/ before landing.
corrected_fix: Proposed fix is correct as written. One caution: the 1 ms yield caps this loop at ~64k events/s and, more importantly, changes test timing — any lazygit test that pumps more than one batch through `run_until_parked()` must gain an `advance_clock` step, so land the const, the yield and the test updates together.
